content:
marta_gomez: FYI AcmeAuth pinged us — they discovered service debug logs in a customer-facing archive that contained short-lived integration tokens. They say tokens were issued by their staging auth service. Link: https://acme.example/report/18425
acme_support: Confirmed. We rotated the affected tokens on our side at 2024-11-17T15:42Z and revoked any active sessions tied to those tokens. No sign of data downloads from acme->redwood endpoints so far. We will share timeline in ~1h.
secbot: Automated alert: unusual webhook activity from acme-integ id=acme-redwood-01 between 2024-11-17T14:20Z-15:10Z, 6 distinct IPs, 2 successful requests that returned 200 for /callbacks.
alex_kaplan: Good catch. Immediate actions: 1) rotate our vendor service account keys, 2) disable acme webhook integration (safe-fail) and route to fallback queue, 3) capture full request logs for investigation. I'll take 1+2.
jonathan_wu: Agree. Also need to confirm whether vendor had access to any KMS-encrypted objects or just plain logs. If vendor accessed encrypted payloads by presigned URLs we might need to rekey. @acme_support can you confirm access patterns?
acme_support: They only pulled debug logs from a public-ish debug-archive bucket. Those logs contain headers and auth debug dumps, not customer payloads. No presigned URLs were used for those debug archives.
ops_oncall: Rotating keys now: running `rbacctl rotate-service-token acme-integ --force` and `aws iam revoke-session acme-integ` in prod. ETA 7m. Will also add deny policy for any s3:GetObject on customer buckets by that role.
secbot: Audit note: enable object-level logging for debug-archive bucket, set S3 object lock off for now, add lifecycle to move debug logs to KMS-encrypted archive daily.
marta_gomez: Legal/comms: @legal_jr we need guidance on customer notification. Risk currently low, but tokens were present in logs. Suggest draft: notifying customers whose webhook endpoints saw 200 responses in timeframe.
legal_jr: Acknowledged. We'll need to classify impacted customers, prepare 72-hr notice if we escalate. For now label as "security investigation" and hold public statement until we confirm exfil.
alex_kaplan: Post-containment checklist: - full session revocation (done), - force reissue of vendor credentials (in progress), - add RBAC least-privilege: vendor role to webhook-only with deny to KMS and customer buckets, - enable SIEM alert for token-use-from-debug-buckets.
jonathan_wu: KMS decision: if vendor never had presigned URLs or KMS decrypt permissions, no immediate rekey. But rotate any CMKs that have broad grants to vendor service accounts and audit IAM policies. I'll run `kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-integ` and post results.
acme_support: We will provide their internal investigation notes and the full token issuance timeline within 2 hours, including the debug config that caused tokens to be logged. We're changing their staging config to redact tokens going forward.
ops_oncall: Added temporary deny rule and moved debug-archive to a private, KMS-encrypted bucket. Also updated the integration to require signed webhook headers and rotated the webhook secret.
marta_gomez: Thanks. Next steps for Monday: vendor SLA update to require token redaction, mandatory MFA for service account access, quarterly third-party audits, and an integration healthcheck that monitors any token in logs.
alex_kaplan: I'll draft the internal post-incident doc (timeline, root cause, mitigation) and assign owners for remediation items. Tagging this thread for the postmortem.
acme_support: Apologies again. We're treating this as high priority and will share artifacts for your security team to ingest.
secbot: Incident ticket created: INC-20241117-84 (linked). Marking for follow-up audit and closure after external vendor report is received.
jonathan_wu: Closing note: If any customer data access is discovered, escalate immediately to legal + privacy. Otherwise we'll classify as vendor config exposure and proceed with the vendor hardening plan.
